request.spec:
The sheet has a review SLA (settings, days, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED key=review-sla
value=<days>; blank means none). A REVIEW claim whose review day (the sheet's today when it went to
REVIEW) plus the SLA days is before the sheet's today shows review-late yes; the summary counts
such claims.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has a review SLA (settings, days, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED key=review-sla
value=<days>; blank means none). A REVIEW claim whose review day (the sheet's today when it went to
REVIEW) plus the SLA days is before the sheet's today shows review-late yes; the summary counts
such claims.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text: A background wait loop I'd started was stopped when it hit its time limit. It never finished on its own because its `pgrep -f 'bin/e2e'` check most likely matched its own command line. That doesn't affect the result: the real `bin/e2e` run had already finished, and all 4 tests passed. Nothing needs restarting, and the review-SLA work is still done as described above.
